focus: non-defining clause comma intonation (parenthetical drop) · defining vs non-defining rhythm · reduced relatives (dropped 'who is') · 'which' referring to a whole clause · preposition + 'whom'
focus_ar: نبرة الجملة الوصفية غير المحدِّدة (الهبوط الاعتراضي)، والفرق الإيقاعي بين المحدِّدة وغير المحدِّدة، والوصفية المختصرة، و'which' للجملة كلها، و'whom'
arabic_challenge: Non-defining clauses must be spoken as a parenthesis — dropped in pitch and bracketed by pauses. Without that, 'My brother, who lives in Dubai, is visiting' sounds like 'the brother of mine who lives in Dubai (as opposed to my other brothers)'. Arabic doesn't use this pitch-bracketing, so the meaning distinction is lost.

target_sounds: non-defining clause as a dropped parenthesis

isolation.instructions: A non-defining clause is EXTRA information, so speak it like a parenthesis: pause, drop your pitch, say it faster, pause again, then return to your original pitch. 'My brother, // (who lives in Dubai) // is visiting.'
isolation.instructions_ar: الجملة غير المحدِّدة معلومة إضافية، فقلها كجملة اعتراضية: وقفة، اخفض النبرة، أسرع، وقفة، ثم عُد لنبرتك.
practice: My brother, // (drop) who lives in Dubai, // (return) is visiting

pair: my brother, who lives in Dubai, ...
my brother who lives in Dubai ...

sentence_practice: My brother, who lives in Dubai, is visiting us.
Cairo, which is enormous, never sleeps.
My teacher, who is from Canada, speaks Arabic.
daily_drills.record_this: My brother, who lives in Dubai, is visiting us next week. Cairo, which is absolutely enormous, never really sleeps. My teacher, who is originally from Canada, speaks Arabic fluently.
daily_drills.self_check: Say 'My brother, who lives in Dubai, is visiting.' Did you pause, drop your pitch, then come back up?

target_sounds: defining clause: no pause, level pitch

isolation.instructions: A defining clause is ESSENTIAL — it says which one — so there is NO pause and NO pitch drop. It flows straight on: 'The man who lives next DOOR is a doctor.' One smooth unit.
isolation.instructions_ar: الجملة المحدِّدة أساسية — تحدّد أيّهم — فلا وقفة ولا هبوط. تتصل مباشرة كوحدة واحدة.
practice: the man who lives next DOOR is a doctor

pair: the man who lives next door (defining)
my father, who lives next door (non-defining)

word_practice: the man who lives next door
sentence_practice: The man who lives next door is a doctor.
The book I read last week was brilliant.
People who smoke should be careful.
daily_drills.record_this: The man who lives next door to us is a doctor. The book I read last week was absolutely brilliant. People who smoke heavily should be careful about their health.
daily_drills.self_check: Say 'the man who lives next door is a doctor'. Is it one smooth flow with no pause before 'who'?

isolation.instructions: Natural B2 speech often drops 'who is' or 'that was': 'the man standing over there' (= who is standing), 'the letter sent yesterday' (= that was sent). Keep the flow tight — nothing marks the gap.
isolation.instructions_ar: الكلام الطبيعي في B2 يحذف 'who is' أو 'that was': 'the man standing over there'. حافظ على الاتصال — لا شيء يشير للحذف.

pair: the man who is standing there
the letter that was sent yesterday

sentence_practice: The man standing over there is my uncle.
The letter sent yesterday hasn't arrived.
daily_drills.record_this: The man standing over there by the window is my uncle. The letter sent yesterday still hasn't arrived. Anyone interested in joining the trip should call me before Friday.
daily_drills.self_check: Say 'the man standing over there'. Does it flow tightly, with no trace of the dropped 'who is'?

isolation.instructions: 'which' can comment on an entire previous statement: 'He arrived late, which annoyed everyone.' Pause before 'which', drop slightly, and stress the comment: '...which anNOYED everyone.'
isolation.instructions_ar: 'which' يمكنها التعليق على الجملة كلها: 'He arrived late, which annoyed everyone.' وقفة قبلها واخفض قليلاً وانبر التعليق.
practice: He arrived late, // which anNOYED everyone

pair: which annoyed everyone (comments on the clause)

sentence_practice: He arrived late, which annoyed everyone.
She passed easily, which surprised nobody.
It rained all week, which was a shame.
daily_drills.record_this: He arrived nearly an hour late, which annoyed absolutely everyone. She passed the exam easily, which surprised nobody who knew her. It rained solidly all week, which was a real shame for the holiday.
daily_drills.self_check: Say 'He arrived late, which annoyed everyone.' Did you pause before 'which' and stress the comment?

isolation.instructions: In formal English the preposition moves to the front: 'the person to WHOM I spoke', 'the topic on WHICH we agreed'. Stress the question word lightly and keep it smooth — this is writing-like speech.
isolation.instructions_ar: في الإنجليزية الرسمية يتقدّم حرف الجر: 'the person to whom I spoke'. أسلوب رسمي قريب من الكتابة.
practice: the person to WHOM I spoke
the topic on WHICH we agreed

sentence_practice: The person to whom I spoke was very helpful.
The topic on which we agreed was funding.
The house in which she grew up is now a museum.
daily_drills.record_this: The person to whom I spoke yesterday was extremely helpful. The only topic on which we finally agreed was funding. The house in which she grew up is now a small museum.
daily_drills.self_check: Say 'the person to whom I spoke'. Is it smooth and formal, with 'whom' not replaced by 'who'?

mixed_pairs: my brother, who lives in Dubai,
the man who lives next door
the man who is standing there
challenge_sentences: My brother, who lives in Dubai, is visiting us.
The man who lives next door is a doctor.
He arrived late, which annoyed everyone.
The man standing over there is my uncle.
daily_drills.record_this: My brother, who lives in Dubai, is visiting us next week. The man who lives next door to us is a doctor. He arrived almost an hour late, which annoyed everyone. The man standing over there by the door is my uncle.
daily_drills.self_check: Three checks: parenthetical drop for non-defining, smooth flow for defining, and a pause before commenting 'which'.

test_yourself.instructions: Record yourself describing your family and neighbourhood, mixing both clause types. The test is whether a listener can HEAR which information is essential and which is extra.
test_yourself.instructions_ar: سجّل نفسك تصف عائلتك وحيّك، ممزوجًا بين نوعي الجمل. الاختبار: هل يسمع المستمع أي معلومة أساسية وأيها إضافية؟
test_yourself.passage: Let me describe where I live. My flat, which is on the fourth floor, looks out over a small square. The building was designed by an architect whose name I've forgotten, but people who know about architecture say it's unusual. My neighbour, who has lived here for forty years, remembers when the square was a garden. The shop on the corner, which used to be a bakery, is now a phone repair place. The family living above me have three children, which explains the noise. My landlord, to whom I pay far too much rent, refuses to fix the heating. The plumber we called last winter said the pipes installed in the sixties should have been replaced years ago, which nobody wants to hear. Still, the people who live here are friendly, and that matters more than the heating.

sounds_to_check.non-defining (pause + pitch drop): My flat, which is on the fourth floor, / My neighbour, who has lived here forty years, / The shop on the corner, which used to be a bakery, / My landlord, to whom I pay rent,
sounds_to_check.defining (no pause, level): an architect whose name I've forgotten, people who know about architecture, the plumber we called, the people who live here
sounds_to_check.reduced relatives: the family living above me, the pipes installed in the sixties
sounds_to_check.commenting 'which': which explains the noise, which nobody wants to hear
sounds_to_check.formal preposition + whom: to whom I pay far too much rent

scoring_guide.90_100: Audible difference between essential and extra information. Ready for week 12.
scoring_guide.50_69: All clauses sound identical, so the meaning distinction is lost. Repeat days 1-2.
scoring_guide.below_50: Redo days 1-5, practising the pause-drop-pause bracket for non-defining clauses.

for_arabic_speakers: Non-defining = EXTRA info → pause, drop your pitch, speak faster, pause, return. It is spoken like a parenthesis.
Defining = ESSENTIAL info → no pause, no drop, one smooth unit.
This is not decoration: the same words mean different things depending on the intonation.
'that' can only be used in defining clauses; use 'who'/'which' for non-defining ones.
Reduced relatives ('the man standing there') are extremely common in natural speech — practise them for fluency.
supplementary_notes.recording_requirement: Record the 'record_this' line daily; compare day 7 with day 1.
